ambition.goal_beyond: The new flavour becomes a steady seller with a clear reorder decision, because the brand learns which channel and message actually sold bottles.

answers.question: What is the brand and the product?
answers.answer: Small hot sauce brand in the US selling on Shopify (about 600 orders a month) and Amazon; new flavour smoked mango habanero; first batch 3,000 bottles in four weeks

answers.question: What is the goal and budget?
answers.answer: 1,000 sold in the first 30 days; launch budget $5,000 total

answers.question: What audiences and tools?
answers.answer: Email list of 14,000 (Klaviyo, draft access); Instagram 22k followers; Meta Ads MCP connected with live access; Amazon Seller Central only through CSV exports

answers.question: Rules and data home?
answers.answer: No health claims on the label or ads; keep things in a Google Sheet; the owner decides

answers.question: What is unsure?
answers.answer: Whether Amazon will approve the listing in time

research.approach: Practitioners launch a small food brand by sizing what the owned audience can carry before they spend: the email list in stages (teaser to everyone, early access for the most engaged, a broad launch, then reminders to non-buyers), organic social, and only then paid ads on a budget big enough to learn from. They treat marketplace approval as the critical path and start it first, keep a fallback, and put claims on a checked list because food labelling rules separate health claims from other claims. They tag every channel so a bottle can be tied to its source, watch stock daily against the sell-through, and read the result against the existing products to see what was new demand.

steps.name: Write down the claims rules and the brand voice
steps.why: Every email, ad and listing is checked against one list of allowed and banned claims; the owner has banned health claims.

steps.name: Pull past results to size what each channel can carry
steps.why: The 1,000-bottle target can only be split across channels from past campaign, social and ad results.

steps.name: Start the Amazon listing first and keep a fallback
steps.why: Approval time is unknown and sets whether Amazon sells at all in the first 30 days.

steps.name: Tag every channel so each bottle has a source
steps.why: Without source tags the readout cannot say which channel sold the bottles or what a bottle cost.

steps.name: Size the channels and split the $5,000
steps.why: Owned channels are free; paid ads need enough budget to leave Meta's learning-limited state, so the split is a decision, not a default.

steps.name: Build the staged email sequence, posts, ads, page and listing
steps.why: Teaser, early access, launch and reminder emails; posts; ads; a product page; and an Amazon listing, all on the same story and claims list.

steps.name: Launch in order and watch daily
steps.why: Stock, sales by channel and cost per bottle decide daily moves of budget within the rules.

pitfalls.text: Treating Amazon as certain; the listing may not be approved or live in time and the Shopify plan has to carry the target alone.
Spreading a small paid budget over many ad sets so none leaves the learning-limited state.
A single blast to the whole list instead of staged sends, which fatigues readers and wastes the most engaged.
Flavour copy that drifts into health claims such as metabolism or disease benefits.

plan.name: Launch the smoked mango habanero sauce

stages.name: Pin down the launch
stages.goal: Turn the request into a target, a budget, a date, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Fix the story and the claims list
stages.goal: Write one page of brand voice, flavour story and an allowed and banned claims list (no health claims) that every launch asset is checked against.

checks.name: Every brand fact names its source and date
Claims are sorted into allowed and banned, and every flavour or heat descriptor is checked against the banned list

stages.name: Gather past results in the Google Sheet
stages.goal: Pull Shopify orders, Klaviyo campaign history, Meta ad history and Amazon reports into one Google Sheet with totals checked against each source.

checks.name: Orders, email sends and ad spend totals match each source's own totals within 1%
Monthly orders are recomputed from the export and compared with the reported 600
Each missing source is listed with what it would unlock

stages.name: Check the Amazon route is real
stages.goal: Find whether the new flavour is a new ASIN or a variation, what approvals it needs, its current status, and how many days the listing and stock have to be ready before launch. Name a fallback date.

checks.name: Listing status, category and brand approval, and the submission date are each recorded or marked unknown
A date is named after which Amazon is treated as zero for the 30 days and the Shopify plan carries the full 1,000
Bottles set aside for Amazon fulfilment are stated and subtracted from the Shopify stock

stages.name: Check every bottle can be tied to a channel
stages.goal: Check Meta tracking health, source tags (UTM) for emails, posts and ads, and that Shopify orders carry the source, so cost per bottle by channel can be trusted.

checks.name: Meta purchases and Shopify orders from the same last 30 days agree within 10%, or the gap is explained
A source tag is defined for each channel (email segment, Instagram, each ad campaign, Amazon) and tested on a real link
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the plan

stages.name: Size what each channel can sell
stages.goal: Test the channel hypotheses against past results: how many bottles the list, Instagram, paid ads and Amazon can each plausibly carry, with ranges and competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the numbers behind it
Each channel gets a low, middle and high bottle estimate with the past result it came from
The middle estimates are added up against 1,000 and the gap or surplus is stated

stages.name: Rank the launch plans
stages.goal: Turn the sizing into two to four launch plans (channel mix, staged send dates, ad budget split, Amazon timing), each with expected bottles, cost, risk, and how it is measured.

checks.name: Every plan adds up to $5,000 or less including ads, samples and content
Every plan has expected bottles as a range, cost per bottle, risk and how it will be measured
Every plan shows what happens if Amazon is not live by the fallback date

stages.name: Owner chooses the plan and budget
stages.goal: The owner picks the plan, the budget split and the launch date. Ask for the reason when they pass over the top plan and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over plans are in decisions.jsonl
A reason is recorded wherever the top plan was passed over

stages.name: Build the launch assets
stages.goal: Write the staged email sequence as Klaviyo drafts, Instagram posts, Meta ad copy and creative briefs, the product page copy and the Amazon listing, all checked against the claims list. Batch into one review.

checks.name: Every line in every asset is checked against the claims list and none makes a health claim
Ingredients, allergens, size and price match the label text and store
Every link carries its channel source tag
Ads and the Amazon listing pass a platform policy check
The email plan has a teaser, early access for the most engaged, a launch and one reminder for non-buyers, and no more than 8 emails in total

stages.name: Launch in order, each live action approved
stages.goal: Create the Meta campaigns paused and read them back; the owner sends the emails and posts, and submits or updates the Amazon listing. Register each test and the launch date before anything goes live.

checks.name: Every campaign was created paused and read back from Meta with the budget, audience and placements of the chosen plan
Committed spend across all paid items is $5,000 or less
Each test and the launch date are recorded in experiments.jsonl before the first send or ad goes live

stages.name: Watch daily, read the 30 days honestly
stages.goal: Each day read bottles by channel, spend, cost per bottle and stock against the plan; propose budget moves inside the $5,000; at day 30 read the whole launch against 1,000 bottles.

checks.name: Bottle counts come from Shopify orders and the Amazon report, not from ad platform figures
Sales of existing flavours are compared with the same weekdays of the 8 weeks before, to show how many launch bottles are new demand
Spend against $5,000, unsubscribe rate and stock on hand are checked at every read
A channel is called better or worse only with at least 30 orders from it; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each test, record cost per bottle by channel and the Amazon timing, decide the second-batch trigger, and plan the next flavour's launch.

checks.name: Every registered test is closed in experiments.jsonl
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this flavour, this brand or the playbook
A reorder trigger is stated as days of stock left against the supplier lead time

hypotheses.statement: The email list and the engaged segment can carry at least a third of the 1,000 bottles.
hypotheses.test: Orders per 1,000 delivered from the last three product emails, the 30 and 60 day engaged segment sizes, and bottles per order.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Past product emails averaged 3 or more orders per 1,000 delivered and the engaged segment is at least 5,000 profiles, so the list gives 330 or more bottles.
hypotheses.refute_if: Past emails averaged under 1 order per 1,000 delivered.

hypotheses.statement: Repeat customers will buy the new flavour more readily than new visitors.
hypotheses.test: Share of the last 6 months' orders from returning customers and their multi-product order rate.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Returning customers are 30% or more of orders.
hypotheses.refute_if: Returning customers are under 15% of orders.

hypotheses.statement: Paid Meta ads can sell bottles at a cost per bottle below its margin, using no more than about half of the $5,000.
hypotheses.test: Past cost per purchase and tracking quality, then a small paused-first test in the first week.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Past or test cost per purchase is below margin per order from the order-margin check, with tracking CHECKED.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cost per purchase is above margin per order, or tracking is UNRELIABLE.

hypotheses.statement: The Amazon listing will be live early enough to sell meaningfully in the 30 days.
hypotheses.test: Listing status, approval needs and submission date from the Seller Central exports and the owner's answer.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The listing is live and buyable at least 14 days before the end of the 30 days.
hypotheses.refute_if: The listing is still pending approval on the fallback date; Amazon counts as zero.

hypotheses.statement: Instagram's 22,000 followers sell bottles directly, not just attention.
hypotheses.test: Orders tagged Instagram or from the link in bio over the last 90 days, per 1,000 followers.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Instagram drove 5 or more orders a month from posts and stories with source tags.
hypotheses.refute_if: It drove under 2 orders a month or cannot be tied to orders.

hypotheses.statement: Part of the new flavour's sales will come from existing flavours rather than new demand.
hypotheses.test: Units of existing flavours in launch weeks against the same weekdays in the 8 weeks before.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Existing flavours' units fall by 10% or more during the launch weeks.

measurement.window: 30 days from launch day, read daily; the first read of paid results after 7 days.
measurement.min_volume: At least 30 orders from a channel before it is called better or worse; Meta ad sets aim for about 50 purchases in the week after their last significant edit or are merged.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause the paid test and ask the owner if cost per bottle is above margin after 7 days, if committed spend would pass $5,000, or if stock on hand falls under the amount that covers the next 7 days.
